overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by entering executive session on a voice vote instead of a roll call, and by minutes recording a roll call that never occurred; it ordered minutes corrected rather than the session redone.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board entered executive session at its May 5 meeting without first taking a roll call vote of its members.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to follow the required procedures for entering into executive session on May 5.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the May 5 minutes falsely recorded a roll call vote to enter executive session when the Board had actually voted by unanimous voice vote.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the minutes are inaccurate because the Board took a unanimous voice vote and not a roll call vote.

allegations.summary: Complainant asked that the Board redo the May 5 executive session; the AG instead chose to remind the Board of the law and correct the minutes.
allegations.key_passage: As the vote to enter executive session was taken in open session and was unanimous, we find it more appropriate to remind the Board of the law's requirements and correct the record of what actually occurred.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Within 30 days of receiving the determination, amend the minutes of the May 5 meeting to show the Board took a unanimous voice vote to enter executive session.
remedy_passage: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and order the Board, within thirty (30) days of receiving this determination, to amend the minutes of its May 5 meeting to show that it took a unanimous voice vote to enter into executive session.
